answer_1.quote: We conducted an extensive review of NLP literature including work in Natural Language Generation (NLG) such as Machine Translation (MT) and Educational NLP (including Grammatical Error Correction and Automated Essay Scoring), but also in Linguistics and Cognitive Science.
answer_1.outputs: explanations for multiple-choice questions across reasoning and language tasks

answer_2.quote: Using two custom agreement metrics, we identified that out of the LLMs, GPT-4o most closely matched our human evaluators.
automatic_metrics: custom hierarchical agreement metric (superlabel and sublabel)

answer_3.quote: we took GPT-4o to act as our third evaluator to enhance the robustness of our analysis, and used it to automatically evaluate the 4,140 explanations from the remaining 360 instances of the annotation set.
methods: structured prompting based on Rubrik rubric
binary judgment (yes/no) on components and dimensions

answer_4.quote: We recruited seven annotators: four general annotators (contractors) and three professionals with experience in language assessment. They were asked to answer a series of multiple-choice questions and explain their choices.
answer_4.guideline: The annotation guide included tasks, examples, and guidelines such as selecting one answer, explaining the choice, time limits, and not revisiting previous tasks.
